Exercise A

Six ways to manage a team

Read the text (about 4 minutes). Then choose the style that each manager is using.

Six management styles

Autocratic (or directive) managers make decisions alone and expect the team to follow instructions. This is fast and clear in a crisis, but people may feel controlled, and the best ideas may never be heard.

Democratic (or participative) managers consult the team and involve people in decisions. Staff feel ownership and give more buy-in, but decisions take longer.

Laissez-faire (or delegative) managers take a hands-off approach. They delegate most decisions and give the team a lot of autonomy. This works well with experienced experts, but a weaker team may drift without direction.

Transformational managers lead with a vision. They inspire people and empower them to go beyond their targets and to grow. The risk: big ideas without enough attention to detail.

Transactional managers focus on clear targets, rules and rewards: meet the target and get the bonus; miss it and there are consequences. This gives structure, but rarely creativity.

Servant leaders put the team’s needs first. They remove obstacles, support and coach. Trust grows, but the manager may find it hard to take tough decisions.

Most good managers do not use one style all the time. They adapt their style to the situation, the task and the people.

Which style is this?

1. When the team is overloaded, the manager does the boring admin and asks: “What’s blocking you, and how can I help?” 1

2. The event director chooses the venue alone and emails the team: “Book it today.” 2

3. The manager talks about making the festival the greenest in Europe and encourages each person to take on a new challenge. 3

4. Before choosing the date, the manager asks every team member for their view, and the team decides together. 4

5. Every stallholder who sells 200 tickets gets a 10% bonus. Anyone who doesn’t loses their place next year. 5

6. The manager tells two experienced planners: “You know this better than I do. Decide, and tell me afterwards.” 6

7. According to the text, most good managers 7.
